analysis.summary: England enter this Group L opener against Croatia as clear favourites, backed by a flawless eight-win qualifying campaign under Thomas Tuchel that produced a 22-0 goal difference and eight clean sheets. Croatia are a battle-hardened side with World Cup pedigree but an ageing core: Luka Modric is 40, Perisic is veteran-level, and the squad is transitioning. England's superior depth, current form, and home-continent advantage in a 60,000-seat indoor stadium make them strong favourites, though Croatia's tactical discipline and big-game experience provide a genuine upset threat.
analysis.home_form: England won all eight UEFA qualifying matches (Group K), conceding zero competitive goals under Tuchel. Results included 5-0 vs Latvia (away), 5-0 vs Serbia (away), 3-0 vs Albania, and a 2-0 home win vs Serbia. Pre-tournament friendlies delivered a 3-0 win vs Costa Rica and a 1-0 win vs New Zealand. Tuchel's side averages 17 shots and 42 box touches per game with a 4-2-3-1 formation. Bukayo Saka is nursing a fitness issue and may not start; Noni Madueke is in contention on the right wing. Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson form a double pivot.
analysis.away_form: Croatia qualified via UEFA Group I with 7 wins and 1 draw, scoring 26 and conceding 4. Run-in included a 4-0 vs Montenegro, 3-0 vs Gibraltar, 3-1 vs Faroe Islands, and 3-2 at Montenegro. Modric overcame a cheekbone fracture in April and is expected to captain and start. Josko Gvardiol returned from a fractured shin in January, making his comeback in May and is expected to be fit to start in a back-three. The squad blends veteran experience (Modric, Perisic, Kovacic) with emerging talent (Baturina, Sucic). Petar Musa, of FC Dallas, likely leads the attack.
analysis.h2h: England and Croatia have met 10 times: England 5 wins, Croatia 3 wins, 2 draws. Most significant meeting: 2018 WC semi-final, Croatia won 2-1 AET (Perisic equaliser, Mandzukic winner after Trippier free-kick). Euro 2020 group stage: England 1-0 (Sterling). Nations League 2018: drew 0-0 then England won 2-1. Croatia have been unbeaten in World Cup meetings (1 match, 1 win). England have won 3 of their last 4 competitive meetings since 2018, suggesting the balance has shifted back.
injuries_news: Bukayo Saka (England) carrying a fitness concern, may not start vs Croatia — Noni Madueke likely starts in his place on the right wing
Tino Livramento (England) withdrew from squad pre-tournament with a calf injury, replaced by Trevoh Chalobah
Reece James (England) only recently returned from hamstring injury, fitness managed
Djed Spence (England) recently returned from jaw injury
Josko Gvardiol (Croatia) returning from fractured shin surgery, made comeback appearance in May, expected to start but with some fitness uncertainty
Luka Modric (Croatia) overcame April cheekbone fracture, cleared to play and expected to captain
key_factors: England's exceptional qualifying campaign under Tuchel — 8 wins, 8 clean sheets, 22-0 GD — shows systemic defensive organization that should suppress Croatia's attack
Croatia's ageing midfield core (Modric 40, Perisic in twilight) faces an athletically superior England midfield with Rice and Bellingham
Gvardiol's injury return is a concern for Croatia's defensive cohesion in a back three — England's pressing and counter-attack could exploit this

Referee Clement Turpin (France) averages ~3.36 yellow cards per match career-wide — this high-stakes opener between two physical European sides could generate cards, though it may fall just short of the 4.5 line
AT&T Stadium is an indoor venue in Arlington — no altitude/heat factor, neutral surface conditions favor neither side
Croatia's big-game resilience: they have reached WC semi-final (2018) and final (2018), and third place (2022) — do not underestimate their ability to stay competitive under pressure
Group L opening match — both sides need points; England will push to win; Croatia may prioritize a point as a realistic away result against a strong England
Tuchel reportedly has history of disputes with referee Turpin (publicly called him 'Grade E'), which is a potential psychological distraction
